title_he: מִי שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל בֶּאֱמוּנָה בְּיֵשׁוּעַ לֹא יֵבוֹשׁ
review: 3:1–3:4 is Luke 11:9–10 in order (שַׁאֲלוּ / דִּרְשׁוּ / דִּפְקוּ — the same three verbs the Arabic uses: اسْأَلُوا / اطْلُبُوا / اقْرَعُوا); the passive תִּנָּתֵן of the verse is kept rather than smoothed to an active 'you receive', and דִּפְקוּ in 4:1 keeps the 'knock' of the door.
5:1–5:2 הַשְׁלִיכוּ עָלָיו מַשָּׂא — Psalm 55:23 (הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל־יְהוָה יְהָבְךָ); the Arabic اطْرَحُوا الْحِمْلَ عَلَيْه is that casting, and the Hebrew keeps the same verb and 'on Him'.

6:3–6:4 the closing wonder-quote is Heb 10:23 (נֶאֱמָן הַמַּבְטִיחַ) as the Arabic's «مَنْ وَعَدْ هُوَ أَمِين» — a participle ('He who promised') with the predicate turned into the analogue of the Arabic's plain adjective, so the Book's own formula reads as the stanza's proof.

1:2 יַעֲנֶה אֶת־דֹּרְשָׁיו — דֹּרֵשׁ is the biblical 'seeker' (Ps 34:11, דֹּרְשֵׁי יְהוָה), chosen over the Modern Hebrew מְבַקְּשָׁיו so the 'seek' of stanza 3 still rhymes back on stanza 1 (דֹּרֵשׁ/דִּרְשׁוּ).

2:1–2:2 the title-line pair opens stanza 2 as the answer to stanza 1; מַאֲמִין ('believing') is the participle the Arabic carries (مُؤْمِنًا), placed before the name so the line keeps the Arabic's cause-before-result order.
